children: , the AI-accelerator and data-center platform leader, faced a fresh edge-computing test as Apple

pushed its new Macs as machines capable of running heavyweight AI privately instead of constantly calling the cloud. Nvidia shares gained approximately 0.7% to $229.08, suggesting investors were hardly treating Apple's move as an immediate threat to the GPU giant's core data-center engine.

Apple showed four Mac Studios working together to run a trillion-parameter model, using shared memory across the machines to tackle workloads once associated almost entirely with expensive server infrastructure. That is an eye-catching demonstration, but the scale gap remains enormous: Nvidia's latest quarter generated $89 billion of data-center revenue out of $96.2 billion overall, meaning roughly 92.5% of sales came from the infrastructure businesses powering large-scale AI. The GuruFocus picture reinforces that underlying strength, with Nvidia carrying a GF Score of 95/100 and particularly strong readings for profitability, growth and financial strength, while GF Value remains the noticeably weaker part of the profile.

The bigger question is not whether a handful of Macs can run a giant model. They clearly can. The question is how much inference, coding and repetitive enterprise AI work permanently shifts from cloud infrastructure onto local machines. Apple could chip away at some private and predictable workloads, especially where data security and recurring token costs matter. But hyperscale training, massive networking demands and unpredictable peak workloads still play directly into Nvidia's territory. For Nvidia investors, the real risk starts only if local AI becomes a structural substitute for cloud inference rather than another layer of the computing stack.

title: Nvidia Gains as Apple Pulls AI Off the Meter
